text.p: Fitch Investor Services said on Monday it affirmed Swedebank's (Sparbanken Sverige AB) A plus long-term deposit rating, F1 short-term deposit and U.S./Euro commercial paper ratings.
"The ratings are based on the bank's well established, nationwide franchise, diversified funding profile and satisfactory earnings capacity," Fitch said in a statement.

"The credit ratings also reflect the strength of AB Spintab, the bank's mortgage subsidiary, which is one of Sweden's leading residential mortgage lenders and a solid contributor to group earnings," the agency said.
"The Swedbank Group is one of the largest financial services providers in the Nordic region," Fitch said.

"Assisted by lower credit costs, earnings have rebounded to adequate levels and continued growth in fee income producing activities brightens future prospects. The repurchase of Robur, an asset manager, has had a significant impact on non-interest income," the agency said. "Going forward, increased operating profits will have a larger impact on the capital position than occurred in 1996."
Fitch said during 1996, much of the rise in operating profits was offset by a return to the payment of standard income tax rates.

"Concerns focus on a still moderately high level of problem loans and interest margin pressures, particularly in bank lending, as a result of rising competition caused by limited business opportunities," said Fitch. "As a predominantly Swedish based financial institution, additional concerns surround the weak domestic economy, which affects Swedbank's primary client base."
"Finally, Swedbank's cost-income ratio, though enviable by European standards, remains significantly higher than its closest competitor, Nordbanken."
Fitch said prospectively, the Swedbank group will be challenged to find new lending opportunities in a stagnant market.
Fitch said it expected this effort to result in Swedbank acquiring significant stakes in competing financial institutions within the Nordic region, much like those carried out in 1996.
